title: 5.1 surround sound
summary: 5.1 surround sound is the most common home theater layout, using five full-bandwidth channels and one low-frequency effects channel for a subwoofer. It originated from early magnetic stereo and Dolby Stereo, with the 5.1 designation formalized in 1987. The system employs front left, front right, center, left surround, and right surround speakers, plus an LFE channel. In music contexts, proper localization for a center-positioned listener requires five matched speakers. The ITU-R BS 775 standard recommends identical speaker size and distance, with specific angle adjustments for movies versus music playback.

mechanisms.title: Channel Configuration
mechanisms.explanation: The system routes distinct audio signals to five full-bandwidth speakers (front left, front right, center, left surround, right surround) and one dedicated low-frequency effects channel typically directed to a subwoofer, enabling spatial separation of dialogue, music, and effects.

mechanisms.title: Speaker Placement and Calibration
mechanisms.explanation: ITU-R BS 775 recommends five similarly sized speakers placed at equal distances from the listener, with front speakers angled ±22.5° for music or ±30° for movies, and surround speakers at ±110°, to ensure consistent localization and equability across all acoustic sources.
